finalists.name: Paycheck Nation (cost-of-living & economic-anxiety explainers)
finalists.case_for: The only candidate in every judge's top 5, with the field's best monetization consensus (8.7 — finance RPM $10-25, corroborated by the meta file's $12-35 band, plus abundant sponsor fit). Backed by the single strongest young-channel proof anywhere in the 28: Edwards Economics went 0 to 358k subs / 12.26M views in ~15.5 months, API-verified with full upload-playlist pagination, with How Money Works (1.72M) proving the ceiling and Wall Street Millennial proving the mid-tier. Fast 2-3/week production cycle means the quickest time-to-YPP of any high-RPM candidate, and the research-brief-to-charts pipeline is a genuinely repeatable system with a clean originality defense (primary BLS/Challenger/Fed data, custom charts).
finalists.case_against: Lowest sustainability among the finalists (5.7): the Edwards template has been publicly visible for 16 months, so a fast-follower field is guaranteed — the attainability judge docked competition to 5 (vs 8/8 from the others) for exactly this. Doom-fatigue risk if the economy improves; news-adjacency means the catalog is less evergreen than the history finalists; some topics skirt 'controversial issues' ad suitability, which could drag realized RPM below the headline finance band; commodity stock-footage look requires the data/charts to carry differentiation.
validation_questions: How far has the window already closed: enumerate channels launched on the Edwards template in the last 6-9 months and measure the view/sub distribution of sub-10k-sub entrants uploading now — do new entrants still get browse distribution in H2 2026?

What is the realized RPM on cost-of-living content specifically: do layoff/affordability topics trigger 'controversial issues' limited-ads (yellow-icon prevalence on comparable videos), and do creator disclosures support $10+ RPM rather than the generic-education $4-6 band?

Does demand survive a macro improvement: measure view decay on 2025-vintage doom-economy videos and test whether evergreen framings (housing lock-in, retirement math) hold views independent of the news cycle?

finalists.name: How Nations Break (economic & demographic collapse history)
finalists.case_for: Best demand evidence in the tournament (consensus 8.0): a 6.0M-view video (Mar 2026) on a channel under 1 year old (Dr. Jonathan Tam, 109k subs/13.3M views in 11 months) plus Fall of Nations (204k subs/43.5M views, created Oct 2024) — recent, repeatable, multi-channel, API-verified proof that the lane admits new entrants right now. Married to the rare combination the business judge prized: finance-adjacent RPM ($8-22) on an evergreen, compounding history back catalog. One-country-per-video is a clean repeatable system with a 100+ topic well, and verifiable-sourcing rigor is a durable differentiator against the arriving AI-slop cohort under the July 2025 policy.
finalists.case_against: The AI-slop crowd is arriving in exactly this lane — factually.co flags Fall of Nations itself as possibly AI — so the differentiation thesis (rigorous sourcing wins over slop) is asserted, not yet demonstrated. Politically charged topics (Zimbabwe, demographics, immigration) invite comment wars, mislabeling, and ad-suitability pockets; accuracy failures are reputationally fatal. The attainability judge scored it a full 1.3 below the other two, noting macro-anxiety dependence and that two breakouts in a hot lane is close to what base rates predict. Higher scripting bar than the disaster lane.
validation_questions: Cold-start census: how many collapse-history channels were created in the last 6 months, what does their view distribution look like, and is the algorithm still distributing to brand-new entrants — or did Tam/Fall-of-Nations close the door?

Does demand extend past the proven marquee cases (Japan demographics, Weimar-tier hyperinflations): keyword-level search and outlier analysis on 20 long-tail country/crisis cases to size the real topic well?

What is realized ad suitability and RPM on politically-charged collapse topics — what fraction of comparable videos run limited ads, and does the hybrid actually land in the $8-22 band rather than pure-history $4-10?

finalists.name: Quiet Catastrophes (forgotten local & industrial disasters)
finalists.case_for: The consensus safe pick: top-3 for all three judges, the lowest judge spread among the leaders (6.60-7.35), the field's best sustainability score (8.0), and zero gate flags. Demand is proven from multiple independent angles, all recent and API-verified: DisastersUncovered (created Dec 2024) pulled 478k views on an Apr 2026 Aberfan video; two channels absorbed 248k and 108k views on near-identical Tenerife videos weeks apart (demand exceeds supply even on covered topics); Fascinating Horror (1.44M subs/315M views) proves the ceiling. Near-zero cost per video (public-domain archives, accident reports), 1/week solo cadence, an effectively bottomless evergreen long-tail well the incumbent hasn't touched, and the attainability judge's #1 — the only candidate whose evidence survived the survivorship-bias screen at full strength.
finalists.case_against: Weakest monetization of the top three (5.7): history/documentary RPM is $4-10 vs $10-25 for the money finalists, tragedy content carries demonetization pockets and advertiser sensitivity, and the somber tone caps crossover virality — this is a lower-variance but lower-ceiling business. Fascinating Horror owns the famous events, so the channel must live in the long tail, where per-video demand below the Aberfan/Tenerife tier is unproven. Growth consensus (6.7) is the lowest among the finalists' demand-side scores.
validation_questions: Does demand hold below the marquee tier: sample 25-30 genuinely long-tail/non-Anglosphere disasters and measure existing coverage and its view performance — is there provable search/suggested demand, or does the audience only show up for famous events?
Base-rate check on the breakout: enumerate all disaster-documentary channels created since 2024 and their trajectories — is DisastersUncovered repeatable or a lottery ticket?

What is realized monetization on tragedy content: yellow-icon/limited-ads prevalence across comparable channels, sponsor participation (VPN/audiobook/Patreon conversion), and whether the calm non-graphic house style demonstrably clears ad review?

finalists.name: The Relocation Report (data-driven US city/state rankings)
finalists.case_for: Ranked #4 on consensus and top-5 for both the attainability and business judges. Search-led discovery is the fairest terrain for a cold-start channel — long-tail relocation queries don't care about subscriber count — and the proof is current: Geography King (270k subs) pulled 203k views in ~3 weeks on a June 2026 upload, with World According To Briggs (1.36M subs, 455M views) proving a decade of demand. Cheapest production of any high scorer (public datasets + charts + stock b-roll, 2/week feasible) enables the fast packaging iteration a new channel needs and the fastest path to YPP; purchase-intent audience (moving, real estate, insurance) borrows finance-adjacent CPMs above pure travel.
finalists.case_against: Carries the shortlist's only live policy flag: ranked listicles + stock b-roll + AI VO at 2/week is the exact templated shape the July-2025 inauthentic-content policy targets, flagged independently by two judges — the shown-methodology defense is simultaneously the moat and the compliance requirement, and it must be executed visibly in every video, not claimed. The niche's search results are already flooded with low-quality slop (listicle fatigue), 'worst places' framing risks advertiser sensitivity and community backlash, and sustainability consensus (5.7) reflects the constant temptation-slash-pressure to slide into the clickbait pattern the niche rewards short-term.
validation_questions: Policy stress test: since July 2025, have ranking/listicle relocation channels been demonetized or algorithmically demoted, and what visible originality features distinguish monetized survivors — does on-screen methodology demonstrably protect?
Saturation measurement: how many active relocation-ranking channels upload weekly right now, and what does the first-90-day view distribution of 2026-launched entrants look like?

Monetization verification: does moving/cost-of-living ranking content actually realize finance-adjacent RPM ($7+) rather than the travel band ($3-8), and are relocation/insurance sponsors accessible to sub-50k-sub channels?

finalists.name: Modern Fraud Files (2020s financial-crime case documentaries)
finalists.case_for: The robustness pick, preferred over higher-mean C17/C11 because it is solid in all three lenses with no factual disputes and no policy flags. The business judge called it the best SYSTEM in the field: DOJ/SEC press releases are a free, legally safe, self-refilling story pipeline — research risk and defamation risk are engineered out by covering only adjudicated cases. True-crime watch time at finance RPM, plus the sharpest sponsor fit anywhere (identity protection, fraud monitoring, VPNs specifically buy scam-aware audiences). An unprecedented 2020s backlog (crypto, PPP, fintech) that incumbents haven't systematically covered, an evergreen compounding back catalog, and a 366k-sub channel currently pulling 87-93k views per fraud story (API-verified) prove the appetite.
finalists.case_against: The weakest attainability evidence among the finalists (competition consensus 5.3): no young-channel breakout was verified in this exact case-file format — the demand proof comes from established channels (WSM, FINAiUS, MagnatesMedia), so the new-entrant thesis rests on the sub-niche gap being real rather than demonstrated. Coffeezilla and news channels own breaking scandals, forcing 'case closed' retrospective positioning whose search tail is unproven; whether true-crime audiences accept AI-narrated finance documentaries is explicitly unverified; some crime-content ad-suitability sensitivity.
validation_questions: Is there any verified sub-2-year faceless channel succeeding on adjudicated-fraud case files — and if not, is the gap opportunity or absence of demand: test search volume and existing-coverage views for 20 named DOJ/SEC cases from 2022-2025?
Do closed-case retrospectives hold demand 1-3 years after the headlines, or do views concentrate at scandal-break (Coffeezilla's territory) — measure the view tail on older fraud documentaries?
Does AI-narrated true-crime-finance retain viewers: compare retention proxies and performance of faceless/AI-VO fraud videos against voiced incumbents covering the same cases?

eliminated_notables:
**C17 Salvage & Sinking Forensics (6.67, rank 5 by mean)** — The highest-scoring cut, excluded on the robustness rule. Its headline attainability proof — Waterline Salvage, created 2025-11, 831k views on 14 videos — was identified by the attainability judge as the incumbent Waterline network's own cross-promoted spinoff, not a cold start, which guts the new-entrant thesis. The 1.55 judge spread (7.35 demand vs 5.80 attainability) is the widest among the leaders, and the disagreement is factual rather than philosophical. If Phase 3 incidentally confirms Waterline Salvage is genuinely independent, C17 re-enters consideration; the niche fundamentals (monthly MAIB/NTSB report pipeline, near-zero fad risk, mariner core audience) are otherwise strong.

**C11 You Wake Up In... (6.65, rank 6)** — The most extreme cold-start proof in the field (George's History: channel created 2025-12-25, 947k-view video 6 weeks later) but spiky where it matters: every proof point is medieval Europe while the pitch's whole differentiation is non-medieval eras whose demand the researcher explicitly labels unproven inference; monetization (5.3) and sustainability (5.3) are the weakest among the top seven; the business judge left it out of his top 5 on weak sponsor surface and no moat; and the same algorithmic openness that produced the proof guarantees a copycat flood. It also carries an AI-imagery templated-format WARN. A strong Plan-B whose validation question — does the format transfer to Edo Japan / Rome / USSR — could be tested cheaply inside another channel's roadmap.

**C12 The Accurate Sleep Historian (6.30, rank 12)** — Highest raw demand score in the tournament (8.3) and the field's best watch-time economics, eliminated because all three judges independently flagged the same uninsurable risk: it launches into the exact genre 404 Media documented as an AI-slop flood, where inauthentic-content enforcement is channel-level and genre-wide algorithmic demotion would destroy the channel regardless of its genuine human-scripted quality. The only candidate where the platform itself is effectively the counterparty; sustainability consensus of 3.7 tells the story.

**C20 Final Report (6.15)** — Explosive verified unit economics (Green Dot: ~1.2M views/video), but they belong to a 2021 entrant into what its own researcher calls the most saturated lane scanned; competition consensus 3.7 is among the field's worst, and the long-tail pivot thesis (non-Western/GA/fresh reports) is admitted unverified inference with structurally lower views.

**C15 Private Equity Autopsies (6.53) / C14 White-Collar Recession (6.37)** — Both business-judge favorites on monetization (8.0 each) but neither has a young-channel proof: C15's headline numbers come from a senator's channel and CNBC (institutional reach, not organic niche demand); C14's views are scattered across news giants with no faceless channel owning the beat, plus thesis risk if the AI-layoffs narrative deflates (sustainability 4.0). C13 dominates both in the same money lane.

**C25 Everyday English (6.58)** — Highest production simplicity (8.7) and real multi-channel proof, but monetization consensus of 4.0 (global ESL audience, $1-4 RPM) makes it a volume treadmill, and two judges flagged it as the field's closest pattern to the inauthentic-content definition.

**C26 AI-at-Work Tutorials (6.27) / C03 Agentic Dev Weekly (6.18)** — Elite monetization (8.0/7.7) wrapped around the field's worst sustainability (3.0 each): tool-churn deletes the back catalog, making the operator buy a treadmill rather than an asset, with C03 additionally in the most crowded, Anthropic-contested lane (competition Δ4, the tournament's biggest disagreement).

**Whole-lane eliminations:** Gaming (C05-C08) died on economics, not evidence — median $3.50 RPM means even C08's 21.8M-view proof channel earns like a finance channel at 3-4M views. C27 was refuted by its own API data (honest senior-health entrants at 221/438 subs while misinfo farms take 3.3M views — proven negative attainability, competition 2.3, the field's lowest). C28's whitespace is not demand (demand 3.7, never verified). C04's view ceiling is demonstrably modest (3.0 demand/growth) — a lead-gen business wearing a YouTube channel.
